renewal_fee_usd.quote: Each application shall be accompanied by a biennial renewal fee of three hundred five dollars.

topical_requirements.quote: The board shall approve one or more continuing medical education courses of study included within the programs certified by the Ohio state medical association and the Ohio osteopathic association under divisions (B)(1) and (2) of this section that assist doctors of medicine and doctors of osteopathic medicine in both of the following: (1) Recognizing the signs of domestic violence and its relationship to child abuse; (2) Diagnosing and treating chronic pain

available.quote: the state medical board may issue, without examination, to an applicant who meets all of the requirements of this section an expedited license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery by endorsement.

requirements.value: Applicant must have passed USMLE/COMLEX steps, held a current unrestricted license from a Canadian province within the past 5 years, actively practiced for at least 2 of the preceding years, meet Ohio medical education requirements, and certify regarding malpractice history, health status, and absence of adverse actions. Ohio is also a member of the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact providing an additional expedited pathway.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fraud during administration of the licensing examination or fraud, misrepresentation, or deception in applying for or securing any license or certificate.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: committed fraud during the administration of the examination for a license or certificate to practice or to have committed fraud, misrepresentation, or deception in applying for, renewing, or securing any license or certificate to practice or certificate to recommend issued by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitting one's name or license to be used by a person, group, or corporation when the individual is not actually directing treatment.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Permitting one's name or one's license or certificate to practice to be used by a person, group, or corporation when the individual concerned is not actually directing the treatment given

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to maintain minimal standards applicable to the selection or administration of drugs, or failure to employ acceptable scientific methods in the selection of drugs or other treatment modalities.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to maintain minimal standards applicable to the selection or administration of drugs, or failure to employ acceptable scientific methods in the selection of drugs or other modalities for treatment of disease

disciplinary_grounds.description: Selling, giving away, prescribing, or administering drugs for other than legal and legitimate therapeutic purposes or a guilty plea or finding related to drug violations.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: selling, giving away, personally furnishing, prescribing, or administering drugs for other than legal and legitimate therapeutic purposes or a plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction of, a violation of any federal or state law regulating the possession, distribution, or use of any drug

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully betraying a professional confidence.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully betraying a professional confidence.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making a false, fraudulent, deceptive, or misleading statement in solicitation of patients or in advertising.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making a false, fraudulent, deceptive, or misleading statement in the solicitation of or advertising for patients; in relation to the practice of medicine and surgery, osteopathic medicine and surgery, podiatric medicine and surgery, or a limited branch of medicine; or in securing or attempting to secure any license or certificate to practice issued by the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: A departure from, or failure to conform to, minimal standards of care of similar practitioners under the same or similar circumstances.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A departure from, or the failure to conform to, minimal standards of care of similar practitioners under the same or similar circumstances, whether or not actual injury to a patient is established

disciplinary_grounds.description: Representing that an incurable disease or injury can be permanently cured with the purpose of obtaining compensation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Representing, with the purpose of obtaining compensation or other advantage as personal gain or for any other person, that an incurable disease or injury, or other incurable condition, can be permanently cured

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtaining or attempting to obtain money or anything of value by fraudulent misrepresentations in the course of practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The obtaining of, or attempting to obtain, money or anything of value by fraudulent misrepresentations in the course of practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: A plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for, a felony.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for, a felony

disciplinary_grounds.description: Commission of an act that constitutes a felony in this state, regardless of the jurisdiction in which the act was committed.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Commission of an act that constitutes a felony in this state, regardless of the jurisdiction in which the act was committed

disciplinary_grounds.description: A plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for, a misdemeanor committed in the course of practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for, a misdemeanor committed in the course of practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: A plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for, a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A plea of guilty to, a judicial finding of guilt of, or a judicial finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for, a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of the conditions of limitation placed by the board upon a license or certificate to practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of the conditions of limitation placed by the board upon a license or certificate to practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to pay license renewal fees specified in the chapter.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to pay license renewal fees specified in this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in division of fees for referral of patients or receiving a thing of value in return for a specific referral.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: engaging in the division of fees for referral of patients, or the receiving of a thing of value in return for a specific referral of a patient to utilize a particular service or business

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of any provision of a code of ethics of the AMA, AOA, APMA, or other board-specified national professional organization.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: violation of any provision of a code of ethics of the American medical association, the American osteopathic association, the American podiatric medical association, or any other national professional organizations that the board specifies by rule

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice according to acceptable and prevailing standards of care by reason of mental illness or physical illness.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inability to practice according to acceptable and prevailing standards of care by reason of mental illness or physical illness, including, but not limited to, physical deterioration that adversely affects cognitive, motor, or perceptive skills.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating or attempting to violate, directly or indirectly, or assisting in or abetting the violation of, or conspiring to violate, any provisions of this chapter or any rule promulgated by the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: violating or attempting to violate, directly or indirectly, or assisting in or abetting the violation of, or conspiring to violate, any provisions of this chapter or any rule promulgated by the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Limitation, revocation, or suspension of an individual's license to practice by another agency responsible for authorizing or regulating health care practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any of the following actions taken by an agency responsible for authorizing, certifying, or regulating an individual to practice a health care occupation or provide health care services in this state or another jurisdiction, for any reason other than the nonpayment of fees: the limitation, revocation, or suspension of an individual's license to practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Revocation, suspension, restriction, or termination of clinical privileges by the US Dept. of Defense or VA, or termination of DEA registration.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The revocation, suspension, restriction, reduction, or termination of clinical privileges by the United States department of defense or department of veterans affairs or the termination or suspension of a certificate of registration to prescribe drugs by the drug enforcement administration of the United States department of justice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Termination or suspension from participation in the Medicare or Medicaid programs.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Termination or suspension from participation in the medicare or medicaid programs by the department of health and human services or other responsible agency

disciplinary_grounds.description: Impairment of ability to practice according to acceptable and prevailing standards of care because of substance use disorder or excessive use or abuse of drugs, alcohol, or other substances.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Impairment of ability to practice according to acceptable and prevailing standards of care because of substance use disorder or excessive use or abuse of drugs, alcohol, or other substances that may impair ability to practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Waiving the payment of all or any part of a deductible or copayment used as an enticement to patients or advertising such waivers.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Waiving the payment of all or any part of a deductible or copayment that a patient, pursuant to a health insurance or health care policy, contract, or plan that covers the individual's services, otherwise would be required to pay if the waiver is used as an enticement to a patient or group of patients to receive health care services from that individual

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to use universal blood and body fluid precautions established by board rules.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to use universal blood and body fluid precautions established by rules adopted under section 4731.051 of the Revised Code

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to cooperate in a board investigation, including failure to comply with a subpoena or order or failure to answer truthfully.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to cooperate in an investigation conducted by the board under division (F) of this section, including failure to comply with a subpoena or order issued by the board or failure to answer truthfully a question presented by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure of a physician supervising a physician assistant to maintain supervision in accordance with requirements of Chapter 4730.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure of a physician supervising a physician assistant to maintain supervision in accordance with the requirements of Chapter 4730. of the Revised Code and the rules adopted under that chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure of a physician or podiatrist to enter into a standard care arrangement with a clinical nurse specialist, certified nurse-midwife, or certified nurse practitioner.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure of a physician or podiatrist to enter into a standard care arrangement with a clinical nurse specialist, certified nurse-midwife, or certified nurse practitioner with whom the physician or podiatrist is in collaboration pursuant to section 4731.27 of the Revised Code

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with standards and procedures established in board rules for the operation of or provision of care at a pain management clinic.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to comply with the standards and procedures established in rules under section 4731.054 of the Revised Code for the operation of or the provision of care at a pain management clinic

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with requirements regarding the drug database for prescribing opioid analgesics or benzodiazepines.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to comply with the requirements of section 4729.79 or 4731.055 of the Revised Code, unless the state board of pharmacy no longer maintains a drug database pursuant to section 4729.75 of the Revised Code

disciplinary_grounds.description: Assisting suicide as defined in section 3795.01 of the Revised Code.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Assisting suicide, as defined in section 3795.01 of the Revised Code

insurance_required.quote: Each person holding a valid license issued under this chapter authorizing the license holder to practice medicine and surgery, osteopathic medicine and surgery, or podiatric medicine and surgery, who is not covered by medical malpractice insurance shall provide a patient with written notice of the license holder's lack of that insurance coverage prior to providing nonemergency professional services to the patient.

establishment_regulation_required.quote: Practicing at a facility that is subject to licensure as a category III terminal distributor of dangerous drugs with a pain management clinic classification unless the person operating the facility has obtained and maintains the license with the classification

definition_quote.value: A person shall be regarded as practicing medicine and surgery, osteopathic medicine and surgery, or podiatric medicine and surgery, within the meaning of this chapter, who does any of the following: (1) Uses the words or letters, 'Dr.,' 'Doctor,' 'M.D.,' physician,' 'D.O.,' 'D.P.M.,' or any other title in connection with the person's name in any way that represents the person as engaged in the practice of medicine and surgery, osteopathic medicine and surgery, or podiatric medicine and surgery, in any of its branches; (2) Advertises, solicits, or represents in any way that the person is practicing medicine and surgery, osteopathic medicine and surgery, or podiatric medicine and surgery, in any of its branches; (3) In person or, regardless of the person's location, through the use of any communication, including oral, written, or electronic communication, does any of the following: (a) Examines or diagnoses for compensation of any kind, direct or indirect; (b) Prescribes, advises, recommends, administers, or dispenses for compensation of any kind, direct or indirect, a drug or medicine, appliance, mold or cast, application, operation, or treatment, of whatever nature, for the cure or relief of a wound, fracture or bodily injury, infirmity, or disease.

drug_authority.value: Physicians licensed under Chapter 4731 may prescribe, personally furnish, administer, and dispense drugs within therapeutic purposes. Prescribing controlled substances requires compliance with DEA registration and drug database requirements. Opioid analgesics and benzodiazepines require database checks before prescribing. Physicians may recommend medical marijuana with a separate certificate to recommend.
drug_authority.quote: Prescribes, advises, recommends, administers, or dispenses for compensation of any kind, direct or indirect, a drug or medicine, appliance, mold or cast, application, operation, or treatment, of whatever nature, for the cure or relief of a wound, fracture or bodily injury, infirmity, or disease.

value: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact expedited license
license_status_types.quote: An individual who holds a current, valid license issued under this chapter and who retires voluntarily from the practice of medicine and surgery, osteopathic medicine and surgery, or podiatric medicine and surgery or a limited branch of medicine may request that the state medical board place the individual's license on retired status.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must hold certification from the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) and have completed not less than twenty-four months of graduate medical education through the second-year level, or be qualified graduates of a fifth pathway training program with twelve months of subsequent graduate medical education. English proficiency must be demonstrated by passing a board-specified examination unless the ECFMG already required it.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Hold certification from the educational commission for foreign medical graduates and have successfully completed not less than twenty-four months of graduate medical education through the second-year level of graduate medical education or its equivalent as determined by the board

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: have successfully completed not less than twelve months of graduate medical education through the first-year level of graduate medical education or its equivalent as determined by the board

pain_management_education_required.quote: The board shall approve one or more continuing medical education courses of study included within the programs certified by the Ohio state medical association and the Ohio osteopathic association under divisions (B)(1) and (2) of this section that assist doctors of medicine and doctors of osteopathic medicine in both of the following: (1) Recognizing the signs of domestic violence and its relationship to child abuse; (2) Diagnosing and treating chronic pain

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: Before prescribing opioid analgesics, physicians must check the drug database unless certain exceptions apply (prescription for 7 days or less; cancer treatment; hospice/terminal patients; hospital/nursing home administration; acute surgical pain). Physicians prescribing to minors must comply with section 3719.061 before issuing opioid analgesic prescriptions.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: a physician shall comply with all of the following as conditions of prescribing a drug that is either an opioid analgesic or a benzodiazepine, or personally furnishing a complete or partial supply of such a drug, as part of a patient's course of treatment for a particular condition

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: in the case of an applicant who prescribes or personally furnishes opioid analgesics or benzodiazepines, as defined in section 3719.01 of the Revised Code, the applicant shall certify to the board whether the applicant has been granted access to the drug database established and maintained by the state board of pharmacy pursuant to section 4729.75 of the Revised Code.

pain_management_clinic_registration_requ.quote: Practicing at a facility that is subject to licensure as a category III terminal distributor of dangerous drugs with a pain management clinic classification unless the person operating the facility has obtained and maintains the license with the classification

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: The state medical board must adopt rules governing prescribing to patients seen only via telehealth. For non-controlled substances, telehealth prescribing is permitted when technology permits a medical evaluation and collection of relevant clinical history consistent with minimal in-person standards of care. For controlled substances, rules must be consistent with federal law. An initial in-person visit for schedule II controlled substances to new patients may be required, with exceptions for hospice/palliative care, medication-assisted treatment, mental health conditions, or emergencies.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The state medical board shall adopt rules governing the requirements for a physician to prescribe, personally furnish, otherwise provide, or cause to be provided a prescription drug to a person on whom the physician has never conducted a physical examination and who is at a location remote from the physician.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: A physician may provide telehealth services in accordance with sections 4743.09 of the Revised Code.

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The 'Interstate Medical Licensure Compact' is hereby ratified, enacted into law, and entered into by the state of Ohio as a party to the compact with any other state that has legally joined in the compact

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: Failure of a physician supervising a physician assistant to maintain supervision in accordance with the requirements of Chapter 4730. of the Revised Code and the rules adopted under that chapter

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Any insurer providing professional liability insurance to an individual authorized to practice under this chapter, or any other entity that seeks to indemnify the professional liability of such an individual, shall notify the board within thirty days after the final disposition of any written claim for damages where such disposition results in a payment exceeding twenty-five thousand dollars.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Within thirty days after the imposition of any formal disciplinary action taken by any health care facility, including a hospital, health care facility operated by a health insuring corporation, ambulatory surgical center, or similar facility, against any individual holding a valid license or certificate to practice issued pursuant to this chapter, the chief administrator or executive officer of the facility shall report to the state medical board the name of the individual, the action taken by the facility, and a summary of the underlying facts leading to the action taken.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The state medical board shall establish a confidential, nondisciplinary program for the evaluation and treatment of practitioners and applicants who are, or may be, impaired and also meet the eligibility conditions described in section 4731.252 or 4731.253 of the Revised Code. The program shall be known as the confidential monitoring program.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: the board, upon a showing of a possible violation, shall refer any individual who is authorized to practice by this chapter or who has submitted an application pursuant to this chapter to the monitoring organization that conducts the confidential monitoring program established under section 4731.25 of the Revised Code. The board also may compel the individual to submit to a mental examination, physical examination, including an HIV test, or both a mental and a physical examination.

investigational_drug_protection.quote: Except for actions constituting willful or wanton misconduct, a treating physician who recommends or treats an eligible patient with an investigational drug, product, or device in compliance with this section is not liable for or subject to any of the following for an action or omission related to treatment with the investigational drug, product, or device: damages in any civil action, prosecution in any criminal proceeding, or professional disciplinary action.
